new_value: Fixed. Root cause was a two-contract merge conflict, not stale data: 457a8bf68c (q6ko.3) stripped native fields from live ipv6-addresses.json into quarantine, while 48c64007d1 (i72x.6 slice) + generate_ipv6_addresses.py regenerated them to carry UPSTREAM AddrForKey values; the cf6da130bf merge kept the B-side data and the A-side Rust consumer. Python suite (144 tests, B-side) was green; Rust consumer was stale. Fix in rust/lichen-core/tests/ipv6_address_vectors.rs: (1) key_derived_identity test now REQUIRES native_packed on each key_derived_identity vector and pins it byte-equal to the external upstream oracle table, plus asserts addr[8..]!=iid (rejected profile cannot slip), replacing the field-absence tripwire; quarantine-integrity pins on legacy corpus retained; (2) yggdrasil_derivation consumer accepts the regenerated binding_invariant_rejected entry type (binding>=1). Module doc updated to describe the post-regeneration contract. Verification: lichen-core ALL suites green (26 test-result lines, 0 FAILED incl. ipv6_address_vectors 4/4); Python ipv6 suite 144/144 still green; test_vectors.py failures unchanged pre-existing (dao_origin o5bl, density_adaptive, x25519). 3x codereview on kimi-k3: pass1 found optional-check hole + stale comments (fixed: mandatory expect + doc rewrite), security PASS (fails closed on unknown pubkeys, rejected profile double-blocked), edge PASS (binding==1 -> >=1 hardened), final re-review PASS.
